By default, we employ the 0.5B model as the draft model and 72B as the target model, with a temperature of 1. All experiments were conducted on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU with 96 GB of memory, unless otherwise specified. - -### Baselines and Metrics -We compare two lossless verification methods—Token-wise [Leviathan et al., 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192) and Block-wise [Sun et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10444)—using two metrics: *Block Efficiency* (tokens/step) and *Decoding Speed* (tokens/second). -- **Block Efficiency** measures the average tokens generated per serial call to the target model, reflecting intrinsic efficiency independent of hardware. -- **Decoding Speed** indicates tokens produced per second for practical reference, though it depends on hardware and implementation. - ## Lossless and Fast Modes HSD runs in lossless mode by default. It accepts the full draft with probability $`\min\{r^*(\boldsymbol{X}_{1:\gamma}),1\}`$ (Eq. 19), where the capped ratio $`r^*`$ divides the joint ratio $`r(\boldsymbol{X}_{1:\gamma})`$ by its largest value over the shorter prefixes. The output then follows the target model's distribution exactly. Fast mode accepts the full draft with the uncapped $`\min\{r(\boldsymbol{X}_{1:\gamma}),1\}`$ instead. It accepts the full draft at least as often, so it yields slightly more tokens per step, but its output deviates slightly from the target model's distribution. In exact checks on small synthetic distributions, fast mode produced 0.5–3% more tokens per step and shifted the output distribution by 0.06–0.15 in total variation distance. Enable it with `--fast` in `eval_speculative_decoding_llm.py`, or with `fast=True` in `generate`. -Earlier versions of this repository always used the fast rule, because the cap was missing from the full-draft test. Tables 1 and 2 below were measured with that earlier code, so they correspond to fast mode. EAGLE-3 drafts its tree by top-k, so every drafted token has draft probability 1, and with such deterministic drafts no lossless verifier accepts more tokens than token-wise verification (see [Corrections](#corrections)).
